source: (cd lp-fw/fw-esp32c6 && cargo build --target riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf --profile release-esp32 --features esp32c6,test_flash_tears_unaligned) && cargo run -q -p lp-cli -- hardware lpfs preflight --port /dev/cu.usbmodem112201 --table lp-fw/fw-esp32c6/partitions.csv && PORT_DEV=/dev/cu.usbmodem112201 scripts/emu/desk-flash-no-monitor.sh -- flash --chip esp32c6 --port /dev/cu.usbmodem112201 --partition-table lp-fw/fw-esp32c6/partitions.csv --flash-size 4mb --after hard-reset target/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/release-esp32/fw-esp32c6 && scripts/emu/flash-tears-cuts.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem112201 --capture target/validate/flash-tears-unaligned.cap --cuts 50 --min-ms 50 --max-ms 2000 --until '[flash-tears] === SCAN DONE ==='
note: flash part JEDEC id 0x464016 expected (what this board's part answered on its first 204 boots, 2026-10-08); every boot's ft-boot record carries the id it read recording 2 of stem `silicon-esp32c6-2026-10-14-609f0e4c9`: silicon-esp32c6-2026-10-14-609f0e4c9.txt already exists and a transcript is never overwritten (DD51). The stem names the firmware commit, not the machine or the host script that produced this file; `tools`, `source` and `firmware_sha256` here say which those were.

trust.because: the board is the ground truth; nothing models it
a real clock on real flash with real wait states
a scope or a logic analyser on the header pin is the definition of what the pin did
a real host really attaches, or really does not
the real ROM and the real IDF bootloader printed it
real bytes over a real port
